problem: The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation ${y}^{′}={y}^{2}+{x}^{2}.$ Given that the point $(1,1)$ lies on the graph of the function, what is the value of ${{y}^{″}|}_{(1,1)}?$
worked_solution:
To find an expression for the second derivative, we differentiate the equation with respect to $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}^{′})^{′} & =({y}^{2}+{x}^{2})^{′} \\ {y}^{″} & =({y}^{2})^{′}+({x}^{2})^{′} \\ {y}^{″} & =2y{y}^{′}+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the chain rule to compute $({y}^{2})^{′}.$

Now, we substitute the given expression for ${y}^{′}$ into the above and simplify the resulting expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″} & =2y{y}^{′}+2x \\ {y}^{″} & =2y({y}^{2}+{x}^{2})+2x \\ {y}^{″} & =2{y}^{3}+2y{x}^{2}+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the coordinates of our point into the above expression for the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{{y}^{″}|}_{(1,1)} & ={(2{y}^{3}+2y{x}^{2}+2x)|}_{(1,1)} \\  & =2(1)^{3}+2(1)(1)^{2}+2(1) \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$
